mishnayos.summary: There are four main kinds of damage: an ox, a pit, an animal eating (or a person), and fire. Each one is different, but the owner must always guard them, and if they do damage he must pay from his best land.

chunks.en: There are four main kinds of damage:
chunks.st: There are four primary categories of damage:

words.note: Avos means "fathers": the main groups that other kinds of damage come from.

chunks.en: The ox, the pit, the maveh, and the fire.
chunks.explain: Maveh is an animal eating with its teeth, or a person.
chunks.st: The category of Ox; and the category of Pit; and the category of Maveh,
chunks.stMore: which, based on a discussion in the Gemara refers either to the tooth of an animal that causes damage or to a person who causes damage; and the category of Fire. Each of these categories is unique; therefore, the halakhot of one cannot be derived from another.

words.note: A hole someone dug and left open.

chunks.st: and the defining characteristic of the primary category of Maveh is not similar to the defining characteristic of the primary category of Ox.

chunks.st: in which the typical manner of their components is to proceed from one place to another and cause damage,

chunks.en: are not like a pit,
chunks.st: are not similar to the defining characteristic of the primary category of Pit,

chunks.en: which does not move around to do damage.

chunks.st: in which the typical manner of its components is not to proceed from one place to another and cause damage;

chunks.en: I must pay as if I made all of its damage happen.

mishnayos.summary: Some animals are "tam" (not known to do harm), and the owner pays half. Some are "mu'ad" (known to do harm), and the owner pays in full. The mishnah lists which is which.

chunks.en: There are five that are tam, and five that are mu'ad.
chunks.explain: Tam: not known to harm. Mu'ad: known to harm, so pays fully.
chunks.st: There are five damage-causing acts that an animal can perform twice and remain innocuous even when its owner was warned each time to prevent it from doing so.
chunks.stMore: After the third time, the animal is rendered forewarned. In such cases, the owner is liable to pay only half of the damages. And there are five damage-causing acts for which an animal is considered forewarned, at times even if it had never caused damage in that manner. In such cases the owner is liable to pay the full cost of the damage.

words.note: An animal not known to do this harm; the owner pays half.
Warned, known to do this harm; the owner pays in full.

mishnayos.summary: A person is always mu'ad. Whatever damage he does, by accident or on purpose, awake or asleep, he pays in full.

chunks.st: and others incurred damage due to any of these,

chunks.st: and another person incurred damage due to them,

chunks.st: and whoever takes possession of the hay and straw first acquires them for himself.

chunks.st: In the case of one who turns over dung in the public domain

chunks.st: and another person incurred damage due to it,

mishnayos.summary: Two potters were walking one behind the other. The first tripped and fell, and the second tripped over him. The first one must pay for the second one's damage.

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. וְאִם אָמַר לְבַעַל קוֹרָה עֲמֹד,
chunks.en: he does not pay. And if he told the beam carrier, "Stop!"
chunks.st: the owner of the cross beam is exempt from liability for breaking the barrel. And if he said to the owner of the cross beam: Stop,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. וְכֵן זֶה בָא בְנֵרוֹ וְזֶה בְפִשְׁתָּנוֹ:
chunks.en: he must pay. The same is true if one comes with his candle and one with his flax.

mishnayos.summary: Two people walking or running in the street who hurt each other do not have to pay.

mishnayos.summary: Someone chopping wood who makes a chip fly and do damage on someone else's land or in the street must pay.

chunks.he: הַמְבַקֵּעַ בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְהִזִּיק בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,

mishnayos.summary: When two oxen (or people) hurt each other, we see which one did more damage, and that owner pays for the difference: full if mu'ad, half if tam. Rabbi Akiva says a tam ox that hurts a person pays full.

chunks.st: each other,

chunks.st: the respective damages are evaluated, and if one amount is more than the other, the owner pays half the damages with regard to the difference.
chunks.stMore: In other words, the owner of the ox that caused the greater damage pays the other owner half the difference.

chunks.en: If both are mu'ad,
chunks.st: If both oxen were forewarned,

chunks.en: they pay full damage for the extra.
chunks.st: the owner of the ox that caused the greater damage pays the full cost of the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.en: One tam and one mu'ad:
chunks.st: In a case where one of the oxen was innocuous and the other one was forewarned,

chunks.he: מוּעָד בַּתָּם מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם,

chunks.he: תָּם בַּמּוּעָד מְשַׁלֵּם בַּמּוֹתָר חֲצִי נֶזֶק.

chunks.en: A person and a mu'ad ox that hurt each other,
chunks.st: If a person caused damage to a forewarned ox and the forewarned ox caused damage to the person,

chunks.en: A person and a tam ox that hurt each other:

chunks.en: a tam that hurt a person pays half damage for the extra.
chunks.st: If the innocuous ox caused greater damage to the person, its owner pays only half the damage with regard to the difference.

chunks.st: With regard to an innocuous ox worth one hundred dinars that gored

chunks.st: and the carcass of the dead ox is not worth anything,

mishnayos.summary: Sometimes a person pays for what his ox did but not for what he did himself, and sometimes the other way around. The mishnah gives examples.

chunks.en: Sometimes one must pay for what his ox did
chunks.st: There are cases where one is liable for an act of damage caused by his ox,

chunks.en: but not for what he did himself;
chunks.st: but exempt from liability for the same action if he performed it himself.

chunks.en: or does not pay for what his ox did

chunks.en: but must pay for what he did himself.
chunks.st: but liable for his own action.

chunks.en: If his ox embarrassed someone,

chunks.en: he pays. If his ox blinded the eye of his servant,
chunks.st: he is liable. Similarly, if his ox blinded the eye of his slave

chunks.st: or knocked out his slave’s tooth,

chunks.st: or knocked out his tooth,

chunks.st: he is liable to emancipate him, as stated in the Torah (Exodus 21:26–27). By contrast, if his ox injured the owner’s father or his mother,

chunks.en: he pays; but if he hurt his father or mother,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay damages, but if he himself injured his father or his mother,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדִישׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,

chunks.he: חַיָּב, וְהוּא שֶׁהִדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדִישׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: he pays; but if he set a pile on fire on Shabbos,
chunks.st: he is liable to pay damages. But if he himself set fire to a haystack on Shabbat,

chunks.en: he does not pay, because he gets a much bigger punishment.
chunks.explain: He is punished by beis din, so he does not also pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying damages. He is exempt from payment in these cases due to the fact that he is liable to receive the death penalty for injuring his father or mother or for desecrating Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: When we do not know which ox did the damage, or which kind of ox did it, the one who wants to take money from the other must bring proof.

chunks.he: שׁוֹר שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר שׁוֹר אַחֵר,

chunks.st: the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

chunks.en: If two oxen were chasing one ox,
chunks.st: In a case where two oxen, belonging to two different owners, were pursuing one ox belonging to a third person, and that ox was injured by one of the pursuing oxen,

chunks.st: and this one, the owner of one of the pursuing oxen, says to the owner of the other: It was your ox that caused the injury,

chunks.st: or, similarly, in a case where one ox is innocuous and one is forewarned,

chunks.en: the one who was hurt says,
chunks.st: and the injured party says: The

chunks.st: forewarned ox caused the damage, and the injured party is therefore eligible to receive full damages,

chunks.en: and the damager says, "No,
chunks.st: but the one liable for damage says: No; rather, the

chunks.en: the tam did damage."
chunks.st: innocuous ox caused the damage, in which case he is liable to pay only half the damage;

chunks.en: Whoever wants to take money from his friend must bring proof.
chunks.st: in both of the above cases, the principle is that the burden of proof rests upon the claimant.

chunks.en: If the ones that got hurt were two,
chunks.st: If the injured animals were two oxen,

chunks.en: one big and one small,

worth before, and how much he is worth now.
Pain: if he burned him with a skewer or a nail,
even on his fingernail,
a place where it does not leave a wound,
we figure out how much a person like him
would want to get paid to feel this pain.
Healing: if he hit him, he must pay to heal him.
If sores came up on him,
if because of the blow,
he must pay. If not because of the blow,
he does not pay. If it healed and opened again,
healed and opened again,
he must pay to heal him.
If it healed all the way,
he does not need to pay to heal him.

chunks.he: שֶׁבֶת, רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִלוּ הוּא שׁוֹמֵר קִשּׁוּאִין,
chunks.en: Sitting idle: we look at him as if he guards a cucumber field,
chunks.explain: He is paid like an easy job, for the days he could not work.

chunks.en: since he was already paid for
his hand and for his leg.
Embarrassment: it all depends on who embarrassed and who was embarrassed.

words.en: and the one who is embarrassed

chunks.en: Someone who embarrasses a person who is not dressed,
who embarrasses a blind person,
or who embarrasses a sleeping person,
must pay. But a sleeping person who embarrassed,
does not pay. If he fell from the roof,
and hurt and embarrassed someone,

chunks.he: חַיָּב עַל הַנֶּזֶק וּפָטוּר עַל הַבֹּשֶׁת,
chunks.en: he pays for the damage, but not for the embarrassment,
as the Torah says, "And she puts out
her hand and grabs him in an embarrassing way."
He does not pay for embarrassment
unless he meant to.

mishnayos.summary: A person who hurts someone pays for all five things, but an owner whose ox hurts someone pays only for the damage.

chunks.en: This is how a person is stricter than an ox:
chunks.st: This halakha is a stringency with regard to a person who caused injury, compared to the halakha with regard to an ox that caused injury:

chunks.en: a person pays for damage,
chunks.st: The halakha is that the person pays compensation for

chunks.en: pain, healing,
chunks.st: damage, pain, medical costs,

chunks.en: sitting idle, and embarrassment,
chunks.st: loss of livelihood, and humiliation;

chunks.en: and pays for the babies,
chunks.explain: If he made a woman lose the baby she was expecting.
chunks.st: and if he caused a woman to miscarry he also pays compensation for miscarried offspring, as the verse states (see Exodus 21:22).

chunks.en: but an ox pays only for damage,
chunks.st: But in the case of an ox that caused injury, the owner pays only compensation for damage,

chunks.en: and does not pay for the babies.
chunks.st: and he is exempt from paying compensation for miscarried offspring.

mishnayos.summary: Cases when someone who hurts another pays for all five things, and rules about hurting a servant.

chunks.en: Someone who hits his father or his mother
chunks.st: The mishna continues: One who strikes his father or his mother

chunks.en: and did not make a wound on them,
chunks.st: but did not cause them to have a bruise,
chunks.stMore: and therefore is not liable to receive court-imposed capital punishment,

chunks.en: or hurts his friend on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: and one who injures another on Yom Kippur, the punishment for which is not court-imposed capital punishment,

chunks.en: must pay for all of them.
chunks.st: is liable to pay for all of the five types of indemnity.

chunks.en: Someone who hurts an eved Ivri,
chunks.explain: A Jewish servant who works for a few years.
chunks.st: One who injures a Hebrew slave

words.note: An eved Ivri is a Jewish servant who works for six years.

chunks.en: must pay for all of them except sitting idle,
chunks.st: is liable to pay for all of the five types of indemnity. This is except for compensation for loss of livelihood suffered

chunks.en: while the servant works for him.
chunks.st: during the time that the injured slave belongs to the one that injured him.
chunks.stMore: Since the right to the slave’s labor belongs to his master, his inability to work is his master’s loss.

chunks.en: Someone who hurts another person's eved Kenaani
chunks.st: One who injures a Canaanite slave belonging to others

words.note: A non-Jewish servant.

chunks.en: must pay for all of them.
chunks.st: is liable to pay for all of the five types of indemnity.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Canaanite

chunks.en: servants do not get paid for embarrassment.
chunks.st: slaves do not have humiliation,
chunks.stMore: so the one who injures the slave pays only the other four types of indemnity.

mishnayos.summary: It is bad to get into trouble with a deaf person, someone not of sound mind, or a child: if you hurt them you pay, but if they hurt you they don't. A servant and a married woman pay later, once they have their own money.

chunks.en: A deaf person, someone not of sound mind, or a child:
chunks.st: The mishna continues: With regard to a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor,

chunks.en: meeting them is bad.
chunks.st: an encounter with them is disadvantageous.
chunks.stMore: In other words, no favorable outcome is possible for someone involved in an incident with one of these people,

chunks.en: If you hurt them, you pay,
chunks.st: since one who injures them is liable.

chunks.en: and if they hurt others, they don't pay.
chunks.st: But if they were the ones who injured others, they are exempt.
chunks.stMore: This is because they lack awareness and are not responsible for their actions.

chunks.en: A servant and a woman:
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to a slave and a married woman,

chunks.en: meeting them is bad.
chunks.st: an encounter with them is disadvantageous,

chunks.en: If you hurt them, you pay,
chunks.st: since one who injures them is liable.

chunks.en: and if they hurt others,
chunks.st: But if they were the ones who injured others,

chunks.en: they don't pay now, but they pay later.
chunks.explain: Right now they have no money of their own.
chunks.st: they are exempt, because they do not have money with which to pay compensation. But they pay compensation at a later time.

chunks.en: If the woman is divorced,
chunks.st: The exemption is only temporary, as, if the woman becomes divorced or

chunks.en: or the servant is set free,
chunks.st: the slave becomes emancipated,

chunks.en: they must pay.
chunks.st: and they then have their own money, they are liable to pay compensation.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who does something so bad that beis din could give him the death penalty does not also pay. And a master who hurts his own eved Kenaani does not pay.

chunks.he: הַמַּכֶּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ וְעָשָׂה בָהֶן חַבּוּרָה,
chunks.en: Someone who hits his father or mother and makes a wound,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: One who strikes his father or his mother and causes them to have a bruise,

chunks.en: or hurts his friend on Shabbos,
chunks.st: or one who injures another on Shabbat,

chunks.en: does not pay for any of them,
chunks.st: is exempt from paying all of the five types of indemnity,

chunks.en: because he is judged with his life.
chunks.st: because he is judged with losing his life.
chunks.stMore: The court imposes capital punishment for these acts, so there is no additional monetary punishment.

chunks.en: And someone who hurts his own eved Kenaani
chunks.st: And one who injures his own Canaanite slave

chunks.en: does not pay for any of them.
chunks.st: is exempt from paying all of the five types of indemnity, because his slave is his property.

mishnayos.summary: How much someone pays for embarrassing a person by hitting or insulting him. Rabbi Akiva teaches that every Jew is important, and tells a story about a man who tried to get out of paying.

chunks.en: Someone who punches his friend
chunks.st: One who strikes another

chunks.en: gives him a sela.
chunks.st: must give him a sela.

words.note: A silver coin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili

chunks.en: a maneh. If he slapped him,
chunks.st: that he must give him one hundred dinars. If he slapped another on the cheek,

chunks.en: he gives him two hundred zuz.
chunks.st: he must give him two hundred dinars.

chunks.en: With the back of his hand,
chunks.st: If he slapped him on the cheek with the back of his hand,
chunks.stMore: which is more degrading than a slap with the palm,

chunks.en: he gives him four hundred zuz.
chunks.st: he must give him four hundred dinars.

chunks.en: If he pulled his ear,
chunks.st: If he pulled his ear,

chunks.en: pulled his hair,
chunks.st: or pulled out his hair,

chunks.en: spat and it reached him,
chunks.st: or spat at him and his spittle reached him,

chunks.en: took his cloak off him,
chunks.st: or if he removed the other’s cloak from him,

chunks.en: or uncovered a woman's head in the market,
chunks.st: or if he uncovered the head of a woman in the marketplace,

chunks.en: he gives four hundred zuz.
chunks.st: in all of these cases, he must give the injured party four hundred dinars.

chunks.en: This is the rule: it all depends on his honor.
chunks.st: This is the principle of assessing payment for humiliation caused to another: It is all evaluated in accordance with the honor of the one who was humiliated, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: even the poor people of Klal Yisrael,
chunks.st: Even with regard to the poor among the Jewish people,

chunks.en: we look at them as if they are
chunks.st: they are viewed as though they were

chunks.en: important people who lost their money,
chunks.st: freemen who lost their property and were impoverished.
chunks.stMore: And their humiliation is calculated according to this status,

chunks.en: because they are children of Avraham,
chunks.st: as they are the children of Abraham,

chunks.en: Yitzchak, and Yaakov.
chunks.st: Isaac, and Jacob, and are all of prominent lineage.

chunks.he: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁפָּרַע רֹאשׁ הָאִשָּׁה בַּשּׁוּק,
chunks.en: Once, a man uncovered a woman's head in the market.
chunks.st: The mishna relates: And an incident occurred involving one who uncovered the head of a woman in the marketplace, and the woman

chunks.en: She came before Rabbi Akiva,
chunks.st: came before Rabbi Akiva to request that he render the assailant liable to pay for the humiliation that she suffered,

chunks.he: וְחִיְּבוֹ לִתֵּן לָהּ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז.
chunks.en: and he made him give her four hundred zuz.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Akiva rendered the assailant liable to give her four hundred dinars.

chunks.en: He said to him, "Rebbe,
chunks.st: The man said to Rabbi Akiva: My teacher,

chunks.en: give me time."
chunks.st: give me time to pay the penalty,

chunks.en: And he gave him time.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Akiva gave him time.

chunks.en: He watched for her standing at the door of her yard,
chunks.st: The man then waited for her until she was standing by the opening of her courtyard,

chunks.en: and broke the jug in front of her,
chunks.st: and he broke a jug in front of her,

chunks.en: and in it was about an issar's worth of oil.
chunks.explain: An issar is a very small coin.
chunks.st: and there was the value of about an issar of oil inside the jug.

chunks.en: She uncovered her head,
chunks.st: The woman then exposed her own head

chunks.he: וְהָיְתָה מְטַפַּחַת וּמַנַּחַת יָדָהּ עַל רֹאשָׁהּ.
chunks.en: and was dipping her hand and putting it on her head.
chunks.st: and she was wetting [metapaḥat] her hand in the oil, and placing her hand on her head to make use of the oil.

chunks.en: He set up witnesses about her,
chunks.st: The man set up witnesses to observe her actions,

chunks.en: and came before Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: and he came before Rabbi Akiva,

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: and he said to him:

chunks.he: רַבִּי, לָזוֹ אֲנִי נוֹתֵן אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז.
chunks.en: "Rebbe, to this woman I should give four hundred zuz?"
chunks.st: Will I give four hundred dinars to this woman for having uncovered her head?
chunks.stMore: By uncovering her head for a minimal benefit, she has demonstrated that this does not cause her humiliation.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "You did not say anything."
chunks.st: You did not say anything, i.e., this claim will not exempt you.

chunks.en: Someone who hurts himself,
chunks.st: One who injures himself,

chunks.en: even though he is not allowed,
chunks.st: although it is not permitted for him to do so,

chunks.en: does not pay. But others who hurt him
chunks.st: is nevertheless exempt from any sort of penalty, but others who injured him

chunks.en: must pay. And someone who cuts down his young trees,
chunks.st: are liable to pay him.
chunks.stMore: In this case as well, the man was liable to compensate the woman for shaming her, despite the fact that she did the same to herself. Similarly, one who cuts down his own saplings,

words.en: and the one who cuts down

chunks.en: even though he is not allowed,
chunks.st: although it is not permitted for him to do so, as this violates the prohibition of: “You shall not destroy” (see Deuteronomy 20:19),

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. אֲחֵרִים שֶׁקָּצְצוּ אֶת נְטִיעוֹתָיו, חַיָּבִים:
chunks.en: does not pay. But others who cut down his young trees must pay.
chunks.st: is exempt from any penalty, but others who cut down his saplings are liable to pay him.

mishnayos.summary: Even after paying, the one who hurt someone must ask him for forgiveness, and the one who was hurt should forgive. If someone says "hurt me" or "break my things," the mishnah explains when the other person still has to pay.

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ,
chunks.en: Even though he pays him,
chunks.st: Despite the fact that the assailant who caused damage gives to the victim all of the required payments for the injury,

chunks.he: אֵין נִמְחָל לוֹ עַד שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ,
chunks.en: he is not forgiven until he asks him,
chunks.st: his transgression is not forgiven for him in the heavenly court until he requests forgiveness from the victim,

chunks.en: as it says, "And now
chunks.st: as it is stated that God told Abimelech after he had taken Sarah from Abraham: “

chunks.en: give back the wife..."
chunks.explain: Hashem told Avimelech to give Sarah back to Avraham.
chunks.st: Now therefore restore the wife of the man; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for you, and you shall live” (Genesis 20:7).

chunks.en: And how do we know that the one who forgives should not be cruel?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that if the victim does not forgive him that he is cruel?

chunks.en: As it says, "And Avraham davened to Hashem,
chunks.st: As it is stated: “And Abraham prayed to God;

chunks.en: and Hashem healed Avimelech..."
chunks.st: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bore children” (Genesis 20:17).

chunks.en: Someone who says, "Blind my eye,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: With regard to one who says to another: Blind my eye, or:

chunks.en: cut off my hand,
chunks.st: cut off my hand, or:

chunks.en: break my leg":
chunks.st: break my leg, and he does so,

chunks.en: he must pay. Even "so that you won't have to pay,"
chunks.st: the one who performed these actions is liable to pay for the damage, despite having been instructed to do so. Even if he explicitly instructed him: Do so on the condition that you will be exempt from payment,

chunks.en: he must pay. "Tear my clothing,
chunks.st: he is nevertheless liable. With regard to one who says to another: Tear my garment, or:

chunks.en: break my jug":
chunks.st: break my jug, and he does so,

chunks.en: he must pay. "So that you won't have to pay":
chunks.st: he is liable to pay for the damage. But if he instructed him explicitly: Do so on the condition that you will be exempt from payment,

chunks.en: he does not pay. "Do this to so-and-so,
chunks.st: he is exempt from payment. If one says to another: Do so, i.e., cause damage,

chunks.en: so that you won't have to pay":
chunks.st: to so-and-so on the condition that you will be exempt from payment, and he did so,

chunks.en: he must pay, whether to his body or to his money.
chunks.st: he is liable, whether the instructions were with regard to the victim himself, or whether the instructions were with regard to his property.

mishnayos.summary: A robber who changes what he stole, like making wood into vessels, pays what it was worth when he stole it. All robbers pay by the value at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: Someone who robs wood
chunks.st: In the case of one who robs another of wood

chunks.en: and makes it into vessels,
chunks.st: and fashions it into vessels,

chunks.en: or wool and makes it into clothes,
chunks.st: or one who robs another of wool and fashions it into garments,

chunks.en: pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: he pays the robbery victim according to the value of the goods at the time of the robbery, but he need not return the vessels or garments.
chunks.stMore: He has acquired the stolen items because they had undergone a change.

chunks.en: If he robbed a cow that was expecting a calf,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a pregnant cow

chunks.en: and it gave birth, or a sheep full of wool,
chunks.st: and it then gave birth while in his possession, or if one robbed another of a ewe that was laden with wool

chunks.he: וּגְזָזָהּ, מְשַׁלֵּם דְּמֵי פָרָה הָעוֹמֶדֶת לֵילֵד,
chunks.en: and he sheared it, he pays the value of a cow about to give birth,
chunks.st: and the robber then sheared it, the robber pays the value of a cow that is ready to give birth

chunks.en: and the value of a sheep about to be sheared.
chunks.st: or the value of a ewe that is ready to be shorn.
chunks.stMore: He pays the value of the animal at the time of the robbery, and the calf or the wool remains his.

chunks.en: If he robbed a cow,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a cow,

chunks.en: and it became pregnant by him and gave birth,
chunks.st: and it became pregnant in his possession, and it then gave birth;

chunks.en: or a sheep, and it grew wool by him and he sheared it,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of a ewe, and it became laden with wool in his possession, and he then sheared it,

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: then the robber pays according to the value of the animal at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: All robbers pay what it was worth when they robbed it.
chunks.st: All robbers pay according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

mishnayos.summary: If what was stolen got older or spoiled, the robber pays its value from when he stole it. But if it only lost value in a way you can't see, he may give it back as it is.

chunks.en: If he robbed an animal and it got old,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of an animal and it aged while in his possession, consequently diminishing its value,

chunks.en: or servants, and they got old,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of Canaanite slaves and they aged while in his possession, they have been changed.

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: The robber therefore pays according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: with servants, he says to him,
chunks.st: With regard to Canaanite slaves, he says to the robbery victim:

chunks.en: "Here is yours in front of you."
chunks.st: That which is yours is before you.

chunks.en: If he robbed a coin and it cracked,
chunks.st: If one robbed another of a coin and it cracked, thereby reducing its value;

chunks.en: fruit and it rotted,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of produce and it rotted;

chunks.en: wine and it turned sour,
chunks.st: or if one robbed another of wine and it fermented,

chunks.en: he pays what it was worth when he robbed it.
chunks.st: then he pays according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery.

chunks.en: If a coin was made no good by the king,
chunks.st: If he robbed another of a coin and it was invalidated by the government;

chunks.en: terumah and it became tamei,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of teruma and it became ritually impure;

chunks.en: chametz and Pesach passed over it,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of leavened bread and Passover elapsed over it, and therefore it is prohibited to derive benefit from it;

chunks.en: an animal that was used for an aveirah,
chunks.st: or if he robbed another of an animal and a sin was performed with it, thereby disqualifying it for use as an offering;

chunks.en: or it became unfit for the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: or if the animal was disqualified from being sacrificed upon the altar for some other reason;

chunks.en: or it was going out to be stoned:
chunks.st: or if the animal was going out to be stoned because it gored and killed a person at some point after the robbery,

chunks.en: he says to him,
chunks.st: the robber says to the robbery victim:

chunks.en: "Here is yours in front of you."
chunks.st: That which is yours is before you.
chunks.stMore: In all of these cases, although the value of the stolen item has been diminished or altogether lost, since the change is not externally discernible, the robber returns the item in its current state.

mishnayos.summary: Workers who ruin what they were given to fix must pay. A builder who breaks the stones of a wall he is knocking down must pay, unless it fell on the other side by itself.

chunks.en: If he gave things to craftsmen to fix,
chunks.st: If one gave items to craftsmen to fix

chunks.en: and they ruined them, they must pay.
chunks.st: and they damaged them, the craftsmen are liable to pay for the damage.

chunks.en: If he gave a carpenter a chest,
chunks.st: For example, if one gave a chest,

chunks.en: a box, or a cabinet to fix,
chunks.st: a box, or a cabinet to a carpenter to fix,

chunks.en: and he ruined it, he must pay.
chunks.st: and he damaged it, he is liable to pay.

chunks.he: וְהַבַּנַּאי שֶׁקִּבֵּל עָלָיו לִסְתֹּר אֶת הַכֹּתֶל,
chunks.en: And a builder who agreed to knock down the wall,
chunks.st: And a builder who committed to demolish a wall

chunks.en: and he broke the stones or did damage,
chunks.st: and while demolishing it he broke the stones, or who damaged them,

chunks.en: must pay.
chunks.st: is liable to pay.

chunks.en: If he was knocking down this side,
chunks.st: If he was demolishing on this side of the wall,

chunks.en: and it fell from the other side,
chunks.st: and the wall fell from another side and caused damage,

chunks.en: he does not pay. But if it was because of his hit, he must pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability. But if a stone fell and caused damage due to the force of the blow, he is liable.

mishnayos.summary: If a dyer ruins wool, he pays for the wool. If he dyes it badly or the wrong color, the Rabbis discuss how much the owner pays him.

chunks.en: Someone who gives wool to a dyer,
chunks.st: In the case of one who gives wool to a dyer

chunks.en: and the pot burned it,
chunks.st: and it was burned in the cauldron during the dyeing process, thereby completely ruining the wool so that there is no enhancement, only loss,

chunks.en: he gives him the value of his wool.
chunks.st: the dyer gives the owner the value of his wool.

chunks.en: If he dyed it ugly,
chunks.st: If he dyed it unattractively [ka’ur] so that the dye is not absorbed well by the wool,

chunks.en: if the gain is more than the cost,
chunks.st: if the enhancement, i.e., the amount that the value of the wool has increased by being dyed, exceeds the dyer’s expenses,

chunks.en: he gives him the cost,
chunks.st: the owner of the wool gives the dyer the expenses.

chunks.en: and if the cost is more than the gain,
chunks.st: And if the expenses exceed the enhancement,

chunks.en: he gives him the gain.
chunks.st: he gives him the value of the enhancement.

chunks.en: If it was to dye it red,
chunks.st: If the owner gave wool to a dyer to dye it red for him

chunks.en: and he dyed it black,
chunks.st: and instead he dyed it black,

chunks.en: or black, and he dyed it red,
chunks.st: or to dye it black and he dyed it red,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he gives him the value of his wool.
chunks.st: The dyer gives the owner of the wool the value of his wool.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if the gain is more than the cost,
chunks.st: Here too, if the value of the enhancement exceeds the dyer’s expenses,

chunks.en: he gives him the cost,
chunks.st: the owner of the wool gives the dyer the expenses.

chunks.en: and if the cost is more than the gain,
chunks.st: And if the expenses exceed the enhancement,

chunks.en: he gives him the gain.
chunks.st: he gives him the value of the enhancement.

mishnayos.summary: A robber who swore falsely that he did not steal, and wants to do teshuvah, must bring the money to the person he robbed, even very far away.

chunks.en: Someone who robs his friend of something worth a perutah,
chunks.st: One who robs another of an item having the value of at least one peruta

words.note: The smallest coin.

chunks.en: and swore to him that he didn't,
chunks.st: and takes a false oath to the robbery victim claiming his innocence,
chunks.stMore: and then later wishes to repent,

chunks.en: must bring it after him, even to Madai.
chunks.explain: Madai was a faraway land.
chunks.st: must bring the money, which includes the principal together with an additional one-fifth payment, to the robbery victim, even if this necessitates following after him to a distant place like Media.

chunks.he: לֹא יִתֵּן לֹא לִבְנוֹ וְלֹא לִשְׁלוּחוֹ,
chunks.en: He may not give it to his son or to his messenger,
chunks.st: The robber may not give the payment to the robbery victim’s son to return it to the robbery victim, and neither may he give it to his agent,

chunks.en: but he may give it to a messenger of beis din.
chunks.st: but he may give the payment to an agent of the court.

chunks.en: And if he died,
chunks.st: And if the robbery victim dies,

chunks.en: he gives it back to his heirs.
chunks.st: he returns it to his heirs.

mishnayos.summary: When a robber who swore falsely must still chase after the person he robbed: only if what is left is part of the stolen money itself, worth at least a perutah.

chunks.en: If he gave him the stolen money but did not
chunks.st: If he gave the robbery victim the principal value of the stolen item

chunks.en: give him the extra fifth,
chunks.explain: The robber who swore falsely adds an extra fifth.
chunks.st: but did not give him the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.en: or he forgave him the stolen money but not
chunks.st: or if the owner forgave him concerning the principal

chunks.en: the fifth,
chunks.st: but did not forgive him concerning the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.he: מָחַל לוֹ עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה
chunks.en: or he forgave him for both,
chunks.st: or if he forgave him concerning this and concerning that,

chunks.en: except less than a perutah's worth of the stolen money,
chunks.st: with the exception of the value of less than one peruta of the principal,

chunks.en: he does not need to go after him.
chunks.st: he need not pursue him to repay the remaining debt.

chunks.en: If he gave him the fifth but did not
chunks.st: By contrast, if he gave the robbery victim the additional one-fifth payment

chunks.en: give him the stolen money,
chunks.st: but did not give him the principal,

chunks.en: or he forgave him the fifth but not
chunks.st: or if the robbery victim forgave him concerning the additional one-fifth payment

chunks.en: the stolen money,
chunks.st: but did not forgive him concerning the principal,

chunks.en: or he forgave him for this and
chunks.st: or if he forgave him concerning this and concerning

chunks.en: that, except a perutah's worth of the stolen money,
chunks.st: that, with the exception of the value of one peruta of the principal,

chunks.en: he must go after him.
chunks.st: he must pursue him to repay the remaining debt.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who swore falsely about money he owes, and then admits it, pays the money, an extra fifth, and brings a korban asham. If witnesses prove it instead, he pays only the money.

chunks.en: He gave him the stolen money,
chunks.st: If the robber gave the robbery victim the principal

chunks.en: and swore to him about the fifth,
chunks.st: and took a false oath to him concerning the additional one-fifth payment, asserting that he had already paid it, then the additional one-fifth is considered a new principal obligation.

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם חֹמֶשׁ עַל חֹמֶשׁ,
chunks.en: so he pays a fifth on top of the fifth,
chunks.st: The robber pays an additional one-fifth payment apart from the additional one-fifth payment about which he had taken a false oath.

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּתְמַעֵט הַקֶּרֶן פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְרוּטָה.
chunks.en: until the main amount is less than a perutah.
chunks.st: If he then takes a false oath concerning the second one-fifth payment, he is assessed an additional one-fifth payment for that oath, until the principal, i.e., the additional one-fifth payment about which he has most recently taken the false oath, is reduced to less than the value of one peruta.

chunks.en: And the same with something left to be watched,
chunks.st: And such is the halakha with regard to a deposit,

words.note: Something one person gives another to keep safe.

chunks.en: as it says, "With a deposit, or with a loan
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against the Lord, and he defrauds his counterpart with regard to a deposit, or with regard to a pledge,

chunks.he: יָד אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת
chunks.en: or with robbery, or he cheated
chunks.st: or with regard to a robbery, or if he exploited his counterpart;

chunks.he: עֲמִיתוֹ אוֹ מָצָא אֲבֵדָה וְכִחֶשׁ בָּהּ
chunks.en: his friend, or he found a lost item and denied it,
chunks.st: or he has found that which was lost, and deals falsely with it,

chunks.en: and swore falsely":
chunks.st: and swears to a lie…he shall restore it in full, and shall add the fifth part more to it” (Leviticus 5:21–24).

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחֹמֶשׁ וְאָשָׁם.
chunks.en: this one pays the money, a fifth, and a korban asham.
chunks.explain: An asham is a korban brought for this kind of sin.
chunks.st: This one must pay the principal and an additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

words.note: A korban brought to make up for certain sins.

chunks.en: "Where is my deposit?"
chunks.st: If the owner asked the bailee: Where is my deposit?

chunks.en: He said to him, "It got lost."
chunks.st: And the bailee said to him: It was lost.

chunks.en: "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: And the owner said: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said, "Amen."
chunks.st: and the bailee said: Amen, therefore accepting the oath;

chunks.en: And the witnesses say that he ate it:
chunks.st: and the witnesses testify about the bailee that he consumed it,

chunks.en: he pays the money.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal.

chunks.en: If he admitted by himself,
chunks.st: If the bailee admitted on his own that he had taken a false oath,

chunks.en: he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal and the additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

mishnayos.summary: If the watchman said the deposit was stolen and swore, and witnesses prove he stole it himself, he pays double. If he admits by himself, he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.

chunks.en: "Where is my deposit?"
chunks.st: If the owner asked the bailee: Where is my deposit, and the bailee

chunks.en: He said to him, "It was stolen."
chunks.st: said to him: It was stolen; and the owner said:

chunks.en: "I make you swear,"
chunks.st: I administer an oath to you,

chunks.en: and he said, "Amen."
chunks.st: and the bailee said: Amen, therefore accepting the oath;

chunks.en: And the witnesses say that he stole it:
chunks.st: and the witnesses testify about the bailee that he stole it,

chunks.en: he pays double.
chunks.st: he must pay the payment of double the principal.

chunks.en: If he admitted by himself,
chunks.st: If the bailee admitted on his own that he had taken a false oath,

chunks.en: he pays the money, a fifth, and an asham.
chunks.st: then he must pay the principal, the additional one-fifth payment, and bring a guilt-offering.

mishnayos.summary: A son who robbed his father and swore falsely, and then his father died, must give the money and a fifth to the other heirs and not keep his share.

chunks.en: Someone who robs his father,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In the case of one who robs his father and the father demands that he return the stolen item,

chunks.en: and swore to him,
chunks.st: and he takes an oath to his father that he did not rob him;

chunks.en: and he died: this one pays the money
chunks.st: and then the father dies; and then the son admits that he robbed him and took a false oath, necessitating the return of the principal and the giving of the additional one-fifth payment to his father’s heirs, of which he is either one of several or the only one; what should he do?

chunks.en: and a fifth to his sons or to his brothers.
chunks.st: This son pays the principal and the additional one-fifth payment to his father’s sons or brothers, and brings a guilt-offering and does not keep his own share.

chunks.en: And if he does not want to,
chunks.st: And if he does not want to forfeit his share

chunks.en: or he does not have money,
chunks.st: or where he does not have sufficient funds to pay the other heirs while forfeiting his share,

chunks.en: he borrows, and the lenders come and get paid.
chunks.explain: They get paid from his share.
chunks.st: he borrows money in the amount of the value of the stolen item and the creditors come and are repaid in part from his share in the stolen item.

mishnayos.summary: If a father makes a vow that his son may not benefit from his things, the son still inherits him. But if he said "in my life and in my death," the son may not inherit.

chunks.en: Someone who says to his son,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his son in a vow: It is forbidden

chunks.en: "Konam, you may not benefit from what is mine":
chunks.explain: Konam is a word used to make a neder.
chunks.st: like an offering [konam], and for that reason you may not derive benefit from my property,

words.note: A word used to make a vow (neder).

chunks.en: if he dies,
chunks.st: if the father then dies

chunks.en: the son inherits him. "In my life and in my death":
chunks.st: the son inherits from him, because it is no longer the father’s property once he dies. The mishna continues: If the father stated in his vow that his son may not derive benefit from his property in his life and in his death,

chunks.en: if he dies,
chunks.st: then even if the father then dies

chunks.en: he does not inherit him,
chunks.st: the son does not inherit from him, as the prohibition is still in effect.

chunks.en: and he gives it back to his sons or to his brothers.
chunks.st: And instead of taking his inheritance, he returns his portion in the estate to his sons or to his brothers.

chunks.en: And if he has nothing,
chunks.st: And if he does not have sufficient funds to subsist without his inheritance,

chunks.en: he borrows, and the lenders come and get paid.
chunks.st: he borrows money in the amount of the value of his share in the inheritance and the creditors come and are repaid from his share.

mishnayos.summary: If someone robbed a ger and swore falsely, and the ger died with no family, the money goes to the Kohanim. The mishnah teaches what happens if the robber dies on the way.

chunks.en: Someone who robs a ger and swore to him,
chunks.st: With regard to one who robs a convert and takes a false oath denying having done so,

chunks.en: and the ger died: this one pays the money
chunks.st: and then the convert dies, the robber, in order to achieve repentance, pays the principal, i.e., the stolen item or, if it is no longer extant, its monetary value,

chunks.en: and a fifth to the Kohanim, and an asham on the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: and an additional one-fifth of its value to the priests, and presents a guilt-offering to the altar,

chunks.en: as it says, "And if
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: the man has no relative to give back the payment to,
chunks.st: But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt,

chunks.en: the payment given back to Hashem goes to the Kohen,
chunks.st: the restitution for guilt that is made shall be the Lord’s, even the priest’s;

chunks.en: besides the ram of atonement that
chunks.st: besides the ram of the atonement,

chunks.en: he will gain atonement with it."
chunks.st: whereby atonement shall be made for him” (Numbers 5:8).

chunks.he: הָיָה מַעֲלֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְאֶת הָאָשָׁם,
chunks.en: If he was bringing up the money and the asham,
chunks.st: If the robber was bringing the money and the guilt-offering up to Jerusalem

chunks.en: and he died, the money is given to his sons,
chunks.st: and he died before paying the priests and bringing his offering, the money shall be given to the robber’s children, and

chunks.en: and the asham grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.explain: A mum is a blemish that makes it unfit for a korban.
chunks.st: the animal designated for the guilt-offering shall graze until it becomes blemished and consequently disqualified from being sacrificed.

chunks.en: and it is sold, and its money goes for nedavah.
chunks.explain: Nedavah: korbanos given as a gift.
chunks.st: And the animal shall then be sold and the money received for it shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

mishnayos.summary: When the robber's money and his korban asham are given to the Kohanim, and in which order. He must give back what he stole before bringing the asham, but the extra fifth can come later.

chunks.en: If he gave the money to the Kohanim of the mishmar,
chunks.explain: A mishmar is the group of Kohanim serving that week.
chunks.st: If the robber gave the money to the members of the priestly watch

words.note: The group of Kohanim serving that week.

chunks.he: וּמֵת, אֵין הַיּוֹרְשִׁים יְכוֹלִין לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָם,
chunks.en: and he died, the heirs cannot take it back from them,
chunks.st: and then died before they sacrificed his guilt-offering, the heirs cannot remove the money from the priests’ possession,

chunks.en: as it says, "A man that
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And every man’s hallowed things shall be his;

chunks.en: gives to the Kohen, it is his."
chunks.st: whatsoever any man gives to the priest, it shall be his” (Numbers 5:10).

chunks.en: If he gave the money to Yehoyariv and the asham to Yedayah,
chunks.explain: Yehoyariv and Yedayah were groups of Kohanim.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If the robber gave the money to the priestly watch of Joiarib and then gave the guilt-offering to the priestly watch of Jedaiah, the following priestly watch, to sacrifice on his behalf,

chunks.en: he did his duty. The asham to Yehoyariv and the money to Yedayah:
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. By contrast, if he first gave the guilt-offering to the priestly watch of Joiarib and then gave the money to the priestly watch of Jedaiah,

chunks.en: if the asham is still alive,
chunks.st: if the animal designated for the guilt-offering is extant,

chunks.en: the Kohanim of Yedayah should bring it as a korban,
chunks.st: then members of the priestly watch of Jedaiah, who received the money, should sacrifice it.

chunks.en: and if not,
chunks.st: But if it is no longer extant because the priestly watch of Joiarib had already sacrificed it,

chunks.en: he goes back and brings another asham,
chunks.st: he should return and bring another guilt-offering;

chunks.he: שֶׁהַמֵּבִיא גְזֵלוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ,
chunks.en: because one who brings back what he robbed before bringing his asham
chunks.st: for one who brings his stolen item to the priests before he brings his guilt-offering

chunks.he: יָצָא. הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא גְזֵלוֹ,
chunks.en: did his duty. If he brought his asham before what he robbed,
chunks.st: has fulfilled his obligation, but one who brings his guilt-offering before he brings his stolen item

chunks.en: he did not do his duty.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he gave the main money but did not
chunks.st: Although he cannot sacrifice the offering before paying the principal, if he gave the principal

chunks.en: give the fifth,
chunks.st: but did not yet give the additional one-fifth payment,

chunks.en: the fifth does not hold him back.
chunks.st: the lack of having given the additional one-fifth payment does not preclude sacrificing the offering.

mishnayos.summary: If a robber's children ate what he stole, or it was left to them, they don't have to pay, unless it was land. We may not take money from tax collectors' boxes, because it may be stolen.

chunks.en: Someone who robs and feeds it to his children,
chunks.st: In the case of one who robs another of food and feeds it to his children,

chunks.en: or left it to them,
chunks.st: or who left a stolen item to them and then died,

chunks.en: they do not have to pay.
chunks.st: the children are exempt from paying the victim of the robbery after their father’s death.

chunks.he: וְאִם הָיָה דָבָר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַחֲרָיוּת,
chunks.en: But if it was something that is like a guarantee,
chunks.explain: Like land, which a lender can collect a loan from.
chunks.st: But if the stolen item was something that serves as a legal guarantee of a loan,

chunks.en: they must pay.
chunks.st: the heirs are obligated to pay.

chunks.en: We may not get change from the box of the customs collectors,
chunks.st: One may not exchange larger coins for smaller ones from the trunk of customs collectors

chunks.en: or from the purse of the tax collectors,
chunks.st: nor from the purse of tax collectors,

chunks.en: and we may not take tzedakah from them.
chunks.st: and one may not take charity from them,
chunks.stMore: as they are assumed to have obtained their funds illegally.

chunks.en: But one may take from inside
chunks.st: But one may take money from the collector’s

chunks.en: his house or from the market.
chunks.st: house or from money he has with him in the market that he did not take from his collection trunk or purse.

mishnayos.summary: When a person may keep things that were taken from others, once the owners gave up hope of getting them back. Also rules about saving a swarm of bees from someone else's field.

chunks.en: If customs collectors took his donkey
chunks.st: If customs collectors took one’s donkey

chunks.en: and gave him a different donkey,
chunks.st: and gave him a different donkey that was taken from another Jew in its stead,

chunks.en: or robbers took his clothing
chunks.st: or if bandits took his garment

chunks.en: and gave him different clothing,
chunks.st: and gave him a different garment that was taken from a Jew in its stead,

chunks.en: these are his,
chunks.st: these items are now his

chunks.en: because the owners gave up hope of getting them back.
chunks.st: because the owners despaired of retrieving them when they were stolen, and they may therefore be acquired by another.

chunks.en: Someone who saves things from a river, or from
chunks.st: In a case of one who salvages items from a river, or from

chunks.en: an army, or from robbers,
chunks.st: a troop [hagayis] of soldiers, or from bandits,

chunks.en: if the owners gave up hope,
chunks.st: if the owners of the items despaired of retrieving them,

chunks.en: these are his.
chunks.st: they are his, i.e., they belong to the one who salvaged them.

chunks.en: And so too a swarm of bees:
chunks.st: And so too, with regard to a swarm of bees,

chunks.en: if the owners gave up hope,
chunks.st: if the owners despaired of retrieving the bees,

chunks.en: these are his.
chunks.st: they are his, i.e., they belong to the one who found them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka said:

chunks.en: a woman or a child is believed to say,
chunks.st: A woman or a minor, whose testimony is not generally accepted by the court, is deemed credible to say:

chunks.en: "This swarm came out from here."
chunks.st: It was from here that this swarm emerged, and it therefore belongs to a certain individual.

chunks.en: And he may walk in his friend's field
chunks.st: And one may walk into another’s field in order

chunks.en: to save his swarm.
chunks.st: to salvage his own swarm of bees that has relocated there,

chunks.en: And if he did damage,
chunks.st: and if he damaged some property in the process,

chunks.en: he pays for what he damaged.
chunks.st: he must pay for what he has damaged.

chunks.en: But he may not cut off his branch
chunks.st: But if the bees settled on a branch of a tree, he may not cut off the other’s branch in order to take the bees,

chunks.en: even if he will pay the money.
chunks.st: even on the condition that he will later give him the money for it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael, the son of Rabbi
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Beroka, says,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:

chunks.en: he may even cut it and pay the money.
chunks.st: He may even cut off the branch and later give him the money for it as compensation.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sees his stolen things in another person's hands, and people know he was robbed, the buyer swears how much he paid and gets that money back. Otherwise, we say he may have sold them.

chunks.en: Someone who recognizes his things and his sefarim in another person's hand,
chunks.st: In a case of one who recognizes his stolen vessels and scrolls in another’s possession,

chunks.en: and people in town were saying he was robbed,
chunks.st: and a rumor had spread in the city that the former had been the victim of theft,

chunks.en: the buyer swears to him how much he paid,
chunks.st: the purchaser, i.e., the one in possession of these items, must take an oath to the victim as to how much money he spent on the purchase,

chunks.en: and takes it. And if not,
chunks.st: and he then takes that sum of money in exchange for returning the items. And if no such rumor had spread,

chunks.en: it is not in his power,
chunks.st: it is not in the purported victim’s power to assert that the items were stolen, and he is not entitled to demand their return,

chunks.en: because I say he sold them to another,
chunks.st: as I could say: The items were never stolen; rather, the purported victim sold them to another,

chunks.en: and this one bought them from him.
chunks.st: and this individual who currently possesses the item purchased them from that other person.

mishnayos.summary: If someone spills out his own wine to save his friend's honey, or lets his donkey go to save his friend's donkey, he gets only a worker's pay, unless he made a deal first.

chunks.en: This one comes with his barrel of wine,
chunks.st: In a situation where this individual came with his barrel of wine,

chunks.en: and that one comes with his jug of honey.
chunks.st: and that individual came with his jug of honey,

chunks.en: The barrel of honey cracked,
chunks.st: if the barrel of honey cracked

chunks.en: and this one poured out his wine
chunks.st: and this first individual poured out his wine

chunks.en: and saved the honey into it:
chunks.st: and salvaged the other’s honey, which is worth more than the wine, by collecting it into his wine barrel,

chunks.en: he gets only his pay.
chunks.st: the owner of the wine has the right to collect only his wage, i.e., compensation for the effort he put into salvaging the honey.
chunks.stMore: He is not, however, entitled to compensation for the wine itself.

chunks.en: And if he said,
chunks.st: But if the owner of the wine said:

chunks.en: "I will save yours, and you
chunks.st: I will salvage your honey

chunks.en: give me the value of mine,"
chunks.st: and you will pay me the value of my wine,

chunks.en: he must give it to him.
chunks.st: the owner of the honey is obligated to pay him compensation for the wine.

chunks.en: A river swept away his donkey and his friend's donkey,
chunks.st: Similarly, if a river washed away his donkey and the donkey of another,

chunks.he: שֶׁלּוֹ יָפֶה מָנֶה וְשֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ מָאתַיִם,
chunks.en: his was worth a maneh and his friend's two hundred,
chunks.st: and his donkey was worth one hundred dinars and the donkey of the other was worth two hundred,

chunks.en: and he left his own
chunks.st: and the individual with the less valuable donkey abandoned his donkey

chunks.en: and saved his friend's:
chunks.st: and instead salvaged the donkey of the other,

chunks.en: he gets only his pay.
chunks.st: he has the right to collect only his wage, i.e., compensation for the effort he put into salvaging his fellow’s donkey.

chunks.en: And if he said to him,
chunks.st: But if he said to the owner of the more valuable donkey:

chunks.en: "I will save yours, and you
chunks.st: I will salvage your donkey and

chunks.en: give me mine,"
chunks.st: you will pay me the monetary value of mine in exchange,

chunks.en: he must give it to him.
chunks.st: the owner of the more valuable donkey is obligated to pay the rescuer compensation for his donkey.

mishnayos.summary: If a robber's stolen field is taken by bullies, it depends: if it happened to the whole area, he gives it back as it is; if it was because of him, he must give a different field. If a river floods it, he gives it back as it is.

chunks.en: Someone who robs a field from his friend, and bullies took it:
chunks.st: In a case of one who robs a field from an-other and thugs [massikin] subsequently take the field from the robber, the halakha is dependent upon the circumstances:

chunks.en: if it is a disaster for the whole land,
chunks.st: If it is a regional disaster in which the thugs seize all the property in the region,

chunks.en: he says to him, "Here is yours in front of you."

mishnayos.summary: If someone robbed, borrowed, or was given something to watch in a town, he may not give it back in the desert, unless that was the deal.

chunks.en: Someone who robs his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one who robs another

chunks.en: or borrowed from him,
chunks.st: or who borrowed money from him,

chunks.en: or his friend left something with him to watch:
chunks.st: or one with whom another had deposited an item,

chunks.en: if in a town, he may not give it back to him in the desert.
chunks.st: if any of these interactions took place in a settled area, he may not return the item to him in an unsettled area,
chunks.stMore: where it is of little benefit to the owner and he cannot safeguard it.

chunks.en: If it was on the deal that they would go out to the desert,
chunks.st: If the loan or deposit was given on the condition that the recipient may go out and return it to the owner in an unsettled area,

chunks.en: he may give it back to him in the desert.
chunks.st: he may return it to him in an unsettled area.
